Right answer to 'what is the literal part of this template', fabricated answer to 'what module does this file depend on'. Found by the lane's own independent oracle (script/lanes/typescript/ts-deriv-audit.ts over script/m14/oracles/typescript-imports-exports.ts, 198 git-tracked corpus files) as ANALYZER-ONLY imports rows: tools/scripts/tsc/generate-enums.ts -> `data:text/javascript;charset=utf-8,:*` and tsc/internal/stringutil/_scripts/generate-unicode-data.mts -> `/:*`. Both name no module in any resolution model. The NEGATIVE half matters as much as the positive: the guard is 'carries a substitution', NOT 'is a template', so a literal template and an ordinary string specifier are still published. Mutants: typescript/imports-computed-specifier-accepted, typescript/imports-template-rejected. The literal-TEMPLATE half is pinned with real backticks and no substitution, because the first version of this fixture used a plain string there and MUTANT B (reject EVERY template, an over-correction) SURVIVED against it. The guard is 'carries a substitution', and only a backtick literal can pin that.
